The Board of Education of Illinois Valley Central Unit School District No. 321 held a regular/ open meeting on Tuesday, August 27, 2024, in the Chillicothe Elementary Center library. President Michael Labeda called the meeting to order at 5:33 P.M.

Board members answering roll call: Mike Birch, Matt Briggs, Brent Cranford, Jennifer Krause, Michael Labeda, Rob Stanley, and Donna Uebler. District Superintendent Chad Allison and Assistant Superintendent Adam Bussard were also in attendance.
MOTION: to enter into closed session at 5:34 P.M, made by Mike Birch, seconded by Matt Briggs, for the following purpose as allowed under the Illinois Open Meetings Act (5
* The appointment, employment, compensation, discipline, performance, or dismissal of specific employees of the public body; and
* Collective negotiating matters between the public body and its employees or their representatives

Return to Open Session – As the Board members and administrators entered the Chillicothe Elementary Center library to return to open session, they were joined by Communications Coordinator Kylie Milliken; District Secretary Jenny Yates; CEC Principal Joe Gallo; Assistant Principal Dustin Birkel and some district teachers and staff.
A motion to return to open session was made by Brent Cranford, seconded by Mike Birch, at 6:44 P.M.
Roll Call: “Ayes” – Brent Cranford, Mike Birch, Matt Briggs, Jennifer Krause, Michael Labeda, Rob Stanley, and Donna Uebler.
Greet Visitors – President Labeda greeted the audience members and visitors watching the live broadcast remotely.
Pledge of Allegiance – President Labeda asked everyone to stand for the Pledge of Allegiance.
Citizens’ Agenda - Opportunity for community and staff input on Agenda Items.
* There were no requests to address the board regarding Agenda Items.

* 2024-2025 District Enrollment Comparison – Dr. Allison shared the enrollment comparison, cohort subtotals. The green highlights show an increase in a specific grade level from last year to this year. For example, we have 160 first grade students in the district this year. Last year we had 142 kindergarten students in this grade level, representing an increase of 18 students. Yellow highlights represent an increase nearing +/- 5 students and red highlighting represents a decrease of greater than 5 students from the 2023-2024 school year.

* County School Facilities Sales Tax Receipts - May 2024 – Dr. Allison shared the County School Facilities Sales Tax Receipts for May 2024 were $78,305. May 2024 was one of the best months on record as it was our second highest receipts thus far since the program began.
* Dr. Allison provided an update regarding the South School Special Education staffing comments

* Dr. Allison addressed Lee Braun’s comments from the August 13th Board member regarding special education staffing at South School. Dr. Allison shared that we are currently in compliance with all state and federal class size and IEP requirements at South and across the district, but we do have some paraprofessional positions posted as we are looking for some additional help.
* Mr. Cranford asked if other districts are short staffed as well. Dr. Allison shared that Dunlap had 21 paraprofessional jobs posted to start the school year.

* Mr. Labeda asked where job postings can be found for the district. Dr. Allison shared that our current job postings are available on the district website and that it will be shared in “Meeting in Review” for tonight’s Board meeting which is shared with all district parents and staff.
* Mr. Bussard addressed the Board regarding community solar.

* Mr. Bussard stated that he had been contacted by Becky Thompson with the option to do a 10-year community solar contract. The district’s participation would save the district an estimated $23,000 annually. He asked if the Board would be interested in a contract of that length.
* The Board agreed to schedule time to meet again for further discussion of a ten-year contract as long as it meant no solar panels would be installed on district property.

* Mr. Bussard also shared his plans to work with Peoria-based IT360 Technology to complete an audit of our technology program and services. IT360 would be interviewing staff, technology department, and teacher leaders to gain a better understanding of our strengths and areas for improvement. They would provide an outside set of eyes to help the district determine how we could improve in all areas of our technology deployment and use.

* Mr. Gallo and Mr. Birkel addressed the Board with an update for the new year. Mr. Gallo shared that the transitioning 6th grade students are doing a fantastic job getting from class to class on time. There has been a positive change with chromebooks being provided to all students in grades 6-8 to be taken home for homework and accessing school websites. So far, it has gone well. Mr. Birkel shared that the Chromebook loaners and repairs have been manageable and the teachers appreciate it too! Reminders from teachers in the morning about charging and other helpful hints have gone well and students are doing a great job!
* CEC Action Statements Aligned to the District Strategic Plan
* The District will continue to make SEL a focus in every classroom and every building in the district - CEC

* Mr. Gallo shared the CEC Action Statements with the Board regarding the strategic plan and their focus on SEL: including SEL focus, Mustang Mornings, Lunch bunch groups, SEL lessons, and Think Sheets. Model Mustangs are specifically tied to the Mustang Mornings and recognizes students doing something well! This month the students are focused on being kind. Mentors are serving as leaders. Dr. Allison also mentioned that volunteers can come to participate in the Mustang Madness! Mr. Gallo shared that staff are always excited to participate and get students involved.
* The district will incorporate ways to welcome new families to the district.

* Mr. Birkel shared information about the Welcoming of new families to CEC. This includes providing building tours, resources online, information on Facebook, a new FAQ page on the district website, timeline information, calendar, etc.

* Typically a new student will be assigned with a student from their homeroom to help them get through the first few weeks. Mr. Gallo shared that giving the tours to the entire family helps the parents see the teachers and students.
* Assess the effectiveness of current elective course offerings at the junior high level.

* Mr. Gallo also shared the work they are doing to help junior high students explore student elective opportunities. More work will be completed during the district’s upcoming early release dates as this work will involve Mossville Junior High as well.

* Dr. Allison shared that the daily schedule at CEC versus Mossville impacts what can and cannot be offered at each school. Ameresco representatives Gene Mackey, Robert Delaney, and Lucas

The Facilities Committee meeting began with Mr. Mackey sharing the site proposal for the district’s 73 acre farmland that is located between South School and IVC High School adjacent to the Chillicothe Public Library. As part of the district’s strategic plan, the following facilities action statements have been developed:
* The District will find an expert to create an analysis of our land to research and provide recommendations on land development.
* The district will develop a plan for relocating the transportation facility. (Priority 1 - December 31, 2024)
* The district will review and identify areas of district facilities where accessibility for all individuals could be improved.

At this meeting the Facilities Committee addressed both priority one action statements above. The District has worked with Ameresco on many recent building renovations has extensive experience in the area of site development for both municipalities and school districts. Ameresco worked with the Architectural Firm of Steckel, Parker, LLC to develop a comprehensive site plan to address the various needs of the school district as outlined in the district’s revised 2024 strategic plan which included 1.) relocating the bus garage (transportation facility); 2.) Addressing the facilities issues that exist at both Chillicothe Elementary Center and Mossville School as identified in the Facility Audit

Ameresco presented Site Plan C in their presentation. The first item on the site plan that was addressed was the bus garage. The bus garage proposal would be an 8,000 square feet garage to address the needs of the district’s fleet. Mr. Birch suggested that possibly two large bays and one smaller bay to allow for maintenance on the district’s minivan and activity buses as well. The terrestrial-based solar field was the second item on the site plan to be discussed. The plan provides for a solar field that would be ground mounted. The estimate from the array would produce enough electricity to provide consumption for both the junior high and the bus garage. General questions regarding the maint

A junior high location was presented next. Mr. Labeda asked if the building should be sized to allow for more than 600 students. The committee requested that the junior high proposal be projected for 800 students as well. Costs and the ability to expand the junior high were addressed as some additional concerns from the committee members.

The next aspect of the plan that was presented was the day care and housing layouts. The group talked about some of the options that could be available regarding housing options and the daycare plan. Finally, Ameresco shared options for additional classroom space at South Elementary as the new junior high would require the move of the fourth and fifth grade students to South Elementary School. This would allow the district to have two pre-K through fifth grade centers with all district 6th through 8th grade students being housed in the new junior high building.

The committee requested that a more formal concept of the bus garage be developed to allow the School Board to consider it as the first step in the site development project. The group talked about looking at the daycare/early childhood education center as the next potential facility to be developed if state grant money still exists for early childhood programs.

Mr. Labeda asked that Ameresco look at how the infrastructure stage and facility construction could be developed in the most appropriate and cost effective manner. Mr. Mackey stated that any development would be created with the best information available to make sure mistakes aren’t made as the development progresses. Mr. Birch also shared his concern that both the Fire District and the City of Chillicothe are approached regarding the district’s future plans and how the City could potentially be involved in the planning of this project.
There were no other items discussed by the Facilities Committee members.
Chairperson Birch asked if there was any further business to come before the Facilities and Transportation Committee. Hearing none, Mr. Birch adjourned the meeting at 6:49 P.M.

The Board of Education of Illinois Valley Central Unit School District No. 321 held a Facilities and Transportation Committee meeting on Thursday, April 10, 2025, in the IVC Central Office Conference Room. Chairperson Mike Birch called the meeting to order at 5:05 P.M.
Committee members present: Mike Birch, Brent Cranford, and Michael Labeda. Board Member Donna Uebler was also in attendance.
District administrators in attendance: Assistant Superintendent Adam Bussard and Superintendent Chad Allison.
The Facilities Committee meeting began with Mr. Birch reviewing the three documents that were included on the meeting agenda.

Mr. Labeda shared that he had been contacted by a Chillicothe Fire Department regarding their interest in the farmland. Mr. Labeda asked if either Dr. Allison or Mr. Bussard had been contacted by them as he had directed them to do. As of the meeting, the Fire District had not contacted either Dr. Allison or Mr. Bussard. It was the consensus of the committee members that they would be willing to talk to the Fire Department about acquiring some land, but the district would proceed with their plan to use the location next to the Chillicothe Cemetery which had been decided previously.

Dr. Allison shared that this was the first cost estimate that had been received by Ameresco in March. Unfortunately, the Board has sold bonds at this point to fund a project that would cost at most $3,000,000. The two options developed by Ameresco were simply not possible for the district at this time. Dr. Allison shared this information with Mr. Birch as the Committee Chairperson. Mr. Birch requested that Ameresco be contacted to see if an itemized cost breakdown could be provided. Ameresco provided that information in early April.

Dr. Allison also shared that he had visited the Macon Meridian School District in January for an IESA state basketball event. Macon-Meridian had just completed a new transportation facility at their high school. Mr. Bussard had contacted their superintendent to see if he would share their costs for that facility. Mr. Bussard shared that the total cost for their two bus garages and a maintenance building and office was $874,888 which included all aspects of the project. This project included three steel buildings, with the drive around the garages and inside the bus garages remaining gravel.

The committee discussed the possibility of a similar layout with our facility as well as our ability to possibly create one large facility because of the amount of land that we have available. The committee was very interested in looking at additional possibilities. Dr. Allison reminded everyone that the one nice benefit of this project was that we do not have a firm “start of school” deadline for completion of this project since our current facility is certainly usable during construction.

The itemized cost estimate was shared with the committee members, but very little seemed to be optional in the cost breakdown. With the cost nearly twice the cost of the Board’s available funds, the Board discussed other options.

Mr. Birch reminded everyone present that the main reason for relocating the transportation department was to address the safety concerns that were identified in the district facility audit from 2022. It was his opinion that we need to see what other options were available to see if a more reasonable facility could be built. Mr. Labeda asked if the buses could be moved to the farmland, while the maintenance garage remained at the current location. Additional safety concerns were discussed by the group resulting in this idea not being considered further.
The committee requested that the district administration provide the general information to some other builders to see if it would be possible to build a new facility with the funds available.
There were no other items discussed by the Facilities Committee members.
Chairperson Birch asked if there was any further business to come before the Facilities and Transportation Committee. Hearing none, Mr. Birch adjourned the meeting at 6:03 P.M.

Citizens’ Agenda - Opportunity for community and staff input on Agenda Items.
* There were no requests to address the Board.
* Back-to-School Update from CEC Principal Joe Gallo and Assistant Dustin Birkel –
* Mr. Birkel shared that the new school year was off to a great start. He mentioned the CEC Buddy Program and Team TRRFC drew great interest from the students.

* CEC is continuing to work on the district’s strategic plan and will be working with the district to review their MTSS Services as they continue to provide a great SEL program, including Mustang Mornings, under the leadership of Kristy Allison. CEC students are encouraged to wear pink this Friday to promote kindness!

* Mr. Birkel also shared some positive comments from the new CEC teachers. They appreciated knowing what to do, and how they are expected to do things throughout the day. One new staff member shared that they can go to their mentor, but don’t have to because every staff person has been so helpful in the building.

* Mr. Gallo shared that there is an increased need to inform students and parents of the importance of attendance. CEC provided handouts during Back-to-School night, and has conversations with parents when attendance becomes an issue. He shared that almost two-thirds of the 8th grade students have perfect attendance thus far. He shared that the school’s problem-solving team meets weekly to help with interventions regarding attendance.

* Dr. Allison shared that the importance of attendance is not a new initiative for the district, but we are working hard to make sure all parents and students understand the importance of good attendance. The district is making a much more concerted effort to educate everyone.

* Mrs. Uebler asked if they had already started sorting the houses for the Mustang Morning program. Mr. Gallo shared that this Friday students will be in homerooms for Mustang Morning to provide some general information and expectations. Friday, September 26th will be the first recognition assembly and the sorting of their houses will take place at that time.

* County School Facilities Sales Tax Receipts - May 2025 – Dr. Allison shared the May 2025 County School Facilities Sales Tax Receipts were $88,102. Dr. Allison shared that it was the 2nd highest month since December 2024.
* August FOIA Report – Dr. Allison shared there were no requests for August.

* 2025-2026 6th Day Enrollment Comparison – Dr. Allison shared our 6th day enrollment numbers for the new school year. He explained that we are down 41 students for this year in comparison to last which is a 2% decrease from the previous year. He shared that the district’s decline over the last five years is actually the lowest percentage in Peoria County. Mr. Labeda asked if Dr. Allison knew why the senior class had experienced such an increase this year. Dr. Allison said he would ask, but did not know.
* Illinois Assessment of Readiness Cut Score Revisions

* “Right-Sizing Illinois’ Proficiency Benchmarks” – Dr. Allison shared the entire presentation that was shared by the State Board of Education. Basically, our cut scores for the Illinois Assessment of Readiness had been adjusted to show a more accurate picture of student and school success across the state. Cut scores to achieve the Proficient level had been decreased for the English/Reading and Math tests, while the science requirements had been increased based on their research.
* ISBE website with revised cut scores – Dr. Allison shared this link which provides a great deal of information regarding the changes.

* ParentSquare Information & Download Links: English & Española – Dr. Allison shared that the ParentSquare implementation is going better than expected. He has received many positive comments from parents. He was impressed by the number of direct messages that have been sent to parents by our teachers. As we get more comfortable with the system, he is hopeful we will continue to improve our communication with parents and the community. Dr. Allison shared links to help parents use the version of ParentSquare that best fits their needs.
* Counslr Information: Parent Guide & Informational Flyer – As a reminder, Counslr app is available to all of our students in grades 6-12 and our staff members.

* School Bus Driver Try-It Day Review – Mr. Bussard shared that they weren’t sure how this event would go, but we did have 8 individuals try driving a school bus for the first time in the high school parking lot. As a result, we have started the hiring process for 2 new drivers who will take over a route once they become licensed. The initial course is offered on September 13th. We plan to do this event more often to let more interested people drive a bus to see if they are interested in becoming a bus driver! Dr. Allison shared that it would be great if there is something we could do to shorten the process of becoming licensed in Illinois, but that is a state issue unfortunately.

* Superintendent’s Report – Mr. Bussard shared a playground update. All three buildings have received their playground sets which have been set in concrete with the curbing done. The pour-in-place surfaces will be completed following the concrete work. Three of the four playgrounds will be fenced. At South there was a bit of a hiccup last Friday night when an unmarked gas was hit during some ground work. Fortunately, it was fixed within an hour to an hour and a half.
* Mr. Bussard and Dr. Allison met with Ameresco and will be looking to schedule a facilities committee meeting to discuss the transportation project.

* Dr. Allison asked Mrs. Moore (Mossville Kindergarten Teacher) if her students had made it through the tough first week. She shared that she may have had the only kindergarten class without tears the first day.
* Dr. Allison reminded everyone that our first home football game is Friday night with the football team and marching band starting their seasons.

* Back-to-School Update from Mossville Principal Pat Sell & Assistant Principal Dr. Cody Pullium – Mr. Sell shared updates from the Strategic Plan which are included on the link above. Mr. Sell shared that they have had a great start to the year with Backpack night, and their Fall Educational night which was held this week. The event included a reading night for pre-k - 5 students, and STEM games for students and parents in grades 6-8. Everyone enjoyed the zoo theme. Approximately 150 parents and students attended the event which was great for a busy Monday night in September!

* Parentsquare has been a great addition to Mossville as a one-stop shop where all activities are easy to find and access anytime. The new playground equipment has been installed, along with new concrete edging and pathways. Once the new ADA accessible surface is installed, the playground will be ready for student use. Mr. Sell shared that this is the first time since he’s been here there is a dedicated pre-k outdoor play area!

* Mr. Sell also shared that this was a great transitional year with MTSS/SEL. Dr. Pullium thanked Communications Coordinator Kylie Milliken for all the help with ParentSquare this year. “SEL bootcamp” was a success again this year which provides students with learning expectations for outside, inside, and bus behavior. The focus of the K-4 morning meeting is the building’s SEL program, Lion’s Quest. The program addresses students’ roles and responsibilities. They are utilizing newsletters and daily announcements for junior high students, as well as lunch group meetings with students to help them be as successful as possible.

* Mr. Sell shared that they are putting a heavy focus on documenting student concerns with students and staff. Making sure students have the resources to get here and be on time. Our resource officers have done a great job following-up with students and parents who have significant absences. Mrs. Uebler asked if they have seen improvements with students getting along. Mr. Sell shared that there are improvements that are evident with our students. He felt that our students have returned to pre-COVID levels.

* Dr. Allison thanked Mr. Sell and Dr. Pullium for handling a threat situation that was posted on TikTok over the weekend. He thanked School Resource Officer Hesterberg as well as the Peoria County Sheriff’s Department and the Illinois State Police for their work in identifying the individuals responsible.

* Counslr: Usage Information; Parent Guide; & Informational Flyer – Dr. Allison shared the usage information for August and thanked the Board for providing this service to our 6-12 students and staff. Parents, students, and staff are reminded that this service is available free, 24 hours per day, 365 days a year.
* Superintendent’s Report – Mr. Bussard shared that the wheelchair lift for the high school gymnasium will be installed September 29th and 30th.

Review and Discussion of transportation center facility options
The Facilities Committee meeting began by reviewing the two documents that were included on the meeting agenda.
Mr. Mackey began the meeting by sharing the following document:
Review and discussion of transportation center facility options

This information included a change from a steel framed structure to a wood framed steel building structure. The core building includes offices, restrooms, storage and five (5) 14’ wide bus bay entries. The proposal included seven additional options with the estimated cost of each option beyond the core building. Each option was discussed as well as the cost estimates that were provided. The overall site proposal also includes a water retention area because the southeast corner of the farmland is approximately 6 feet lower than the northwest corner which is where the public library is located. The overall site location would also allow for an access road to the east of the transportation cent

Mr. Bussard asked if the footprint would be the same regardless of the options that are selected by the Board. Mr. Delaney confirmed that the fencing and exterior perimeter would be the same and any options could be reconfigured inside, but the fencing would never need to be moved. Mr. Bussard also confirmed that an access road would be possible in the future on the east side of the facility.

Mr. Birch asked if the facility would need to be annexed into the city to connect to public utilities and potentially Police coverage. The district will discuss the possibility of annexing the 5 acre location into the city. Mr. Birch also asked about future addition of garage doors and the necessary power to plug-in the bus block heaters. Mr. Delaney confirmed that garage doors could be added in the future and there will be enough electricity to plug in all buses as each module is added.

The committee would like to see a core building layout that would allow for 5 entrances behind the main building with the option to expand on both the east and west sides of the core building. Mr. Bussard will make this request to Ameresco. Additionally, the committee would like a cost estimate to asphalt the driver/visitor parking lot in front of the building.
Mr. Bussard then presented the following information regarding the replacement of the auditorium lighting.
Review and discussion of auditorium lighting

Mr. Bussard shared the lighting concerns that exist in the auditorium. Mr. Bussard shared that the original lights have reached their life expectancy and are becoming a serious safety concern as they are running extremely hot. While the cost estimate to upgrade the lighting is significant (nearly $300,000), the committee members understood the concern and were willing to commit the funds to upgrade the lighting. This is an expenditure that will be paid from school facilities tax revenue.

Mr. Labeda asked if this estimate addressed the sound system in the auditorium as well. Mr. Bussard shared that we had upgraded the sound system last year, so the auditorium will be fully upgraded once the lighting replacement occurs.
There were no other items discussed by the Facilities Committee members.

The Board of Education of Illinois Valley Central Unit School District No. 321 held a Facilities and Transportation Committee meeting on Thursday, March 5, 2026, in the IVC Central Office Conference Room. Chairperson Mike Birch called the meeting to order at 4:05 P.M.
Committee members present: Mike Birch, Brent Cranford, and Michael Labeda.
Other Board Members in attendance: Jennifer Krause, Rob Stanley, and Donna Uebler.
District administrators in attendance: Assistant Superintendent Adam Bussard and Superintendent Chad Allison.
Review and Discussion of revised transportation center facility options
The Facilities Committee meeting began by reviewing and discussing the revisions to the Transportation Facility that were shared by Mr. Bussard.
Mr. Bussard provided a packet of information to the committee members and others in attendance. A link to that information follows:

The first document that he reviewed was the revised facility proposal from Ameresco. The Ameresco revised plan included a 23,000 sf bus storage structure. “While the new structure is over 3.5 times the size of the office/maintenance structure; restrooms, HVAC, flooring, walls, windows, ceilings and interiors are eliminated.” Mr. Bussard shared that the district has sold bonds with a $3.5 million budget maximum.

Mr. Bussard reminded everyone that the initial goal of the relocation of the transportation facility and bus parking more specifically was addressed in the strategic plan and the original district facility audit focused on the safety and security of our buses and the need to have access to our bus fleet in the event of an emergency situation. Additionally, we have been unable to hire a bus mechanic, so we are using a vendor from Princeton to maintain our buses. It is unclear if this is a temporary situation, or if it may become our maintenance model if a district bus mechanic cannot be found.

The breakdown of the Ameresco predicted costs per option were presented: $3,800,000 for the full site with garage enclosure; $3,600,000 for a reduced site with garage enclosure; $3,400,000 for a full site with canopy option; and $3,200,000 for a reduced site with canopy option. The Ameresco proposal does include all site work and the ability for future expansion on the farmland.

Mr. Bussard also shared the information that was provided by Classen Design & Build. Chris Classen from Classen Design & Build offered to provide some general information as an alternative to the Ameresco projections. Mr. Classen requested general cost estimates for both a wood and steel framed storage facility. The estimates provided by Classen Design & Build were for a single 8,000 sf building with 12 - 12’-0” wide overhead doors with an estimated cost of $1,288,650. Two wood frame buildings with the same dimensions was $2,413,950. Additionally, a single metal frame building was estimated at $1,609,300 with two metal frame buildings estimated to be $2,813,250. As provided in the informatio

Based on the information provided, the Committee felt the project proposals provided by Classen Design & Build allowed the district to better meet our goals for moving the facility while meeting our budget target. Mr. Labeda asked if we could just let Ameresco know that they have missed the target on this one. Our previous projects were very positive with Ameresco, but unfortunately we never seemed to be on the same page with this project. The Committee agreed that it was appropriate to thank Ameresco for their work, but they felt we were unable to use them for this project with our budget restraints. The committee asked the administration to discuss getting more specific plans and informati

Mr. Birch wanted to make sure everyone understood that Mr. Classen only had general information in his proposal, so there may be more costs and the total cost of the project may grow closer to our $3.5 million dollar budget. Dr. Allison shared that the Brimfield School District had to bid for their transportation facility three different times as the bids continued to exceed their allotted funds.

The Committee also discussed the location of the two different buildings. The Committee felt it would be best if the buildings were formed in an L-shape with one building running along Cloverdale and the second building along the cemetery side of the farmland.
There were no other items discussed by the Facilities Committee members.
There were no requests to address the committee during public comments.
Chairperson Birch asked if there was any further business to come before the Facilities and Transportation Committee. Hearing none, Mr. Birch adjourned the meeting at 5:19 P.M.
